title: Ways of Making Wealth
note: This chapter tells how to make wealth, which is mostly gained through the country and guarded by the fortress.

couplets.plain: Nothing counts but wealth, which makes people who don’t count into people who do.
couplets.pm: Apart from wealth, which can make those held of no account into people of account, a person has nothing worth the name. Those of no account are the ignorant and the low-born. Wealth makes the wise and the high-born come and stand before them. It alone is what should be earned.

links.quote: makes people who don’t count into people who do
links.reason: Wealth alone can make someone of no account count for something.

couplets.plain: Everyone scorns those who have nothing. Everyone honours the rich.
couplets.pm: Everyone scorns those without wealth, even if they have every virtue. Everyone exalts those who have it, even if they have every vice, by lowering themselves before them. Enemies, friends and strangers alike do this, so he says “everyone”, and he says it twice for force.

links.quote: Everyone honours the rich
links.reason: Shows the honour wealth commands from everyone.

links.quote: Everyone scorns those who have nothing

couplets.plain: The unfailing lamp called wealth goes to whatever land you think of and cuts through the dark.
couplets.pm: The undying lamp all people honour as wealth goes, for those who made it, to whatever land they have in mind, and destroys the darkness of enmity. It is “unfailing” because all need it at all times. Going where you think of marks how it differs from other lamps.

links.quote: goes to whatever land you think of and cuts through the dark
The unfailing lamp called wealth
links.reason: Pictures wealth as a lamp that never fails.

links.quote: cuts through the dark

couplets.plain: Wealth that comes by knowing how, and without wrong, gives birth to righteousness and to happiness.
couplets.pm: Wealth a ruler gets by knowing the proper way to earn it, without cruel rule, gives him righteousness and happiness. Righteousness, because he is praised for a just sceptre and gains merit from worship of the gods and from gifts. Happiness, because it can be enjoyed for a long time. So earn it that way.

links.quote: gives birth to righteousness and to happiness
links.reason: Says both righteousness and happiness are born of wealth gained without wrong.

links.quote: comes by knowing how, and without wrong
links.reason: Keeps its blessing for wealth that comes without wrong.

links.quote: Wealth that comes by knowing how, and without wrong, gives birth to righteousness and to happiness

couplets.plain: Wealth that comes without compassion and loving-kindness: don’t embrace it, let it roll away.
couplets.pm: Rulers should not touch wealth that doesn’t come with the compassion they show their people and the loving-kindness the people show them. Coming with these means coming as the sixth share. Other wealth, like water in an unbaked pot, takes its maker down with it, so he says not only “don’t embrace it” but “let it roll away”.

links.quote: Wealth that comes without compassion and loving-kindness
links.reason: Makes compassion the condition wealth must meet before you embrace it.

links.quote: don’t embrace it, let it roll away

couplets.plain: Wealth that comes to him unbidden, customs dues, and wealth from crushing his enemies: these are a ruler’s wealth.
couplets.pm: A ruler’s wealth is what comes to him because it has no owner, such as treasure found in the ground long after those who buried it have died, or property with no heirs. It is also customs on goods arriving by ship and by land, and tribute taken from his enemies. These are his beyond the sixth share.

links.quote: these are a ruler’s wealth
links.reason: Sets out where a ruler’s wealth comes from: what comes unbidden, customs dues and what he takes from enemies.

couplets.plain: Compassion, the child that loving-kindness bears, thrives with the rich foster-mother called wealth.
couplets.pm: The child compassion, born of loving-kindness, grows up with the foster-mother called wealth. Compassion reaches the suffering without any tie, and it ripens from loving-kindness, which goes by ties. Only those able to end poverty can reach the poor, so wealth is its nurse. Unlike other nurses she supplies everything herself, so she is “rich”.

links.quote: the rich foster-mother called wealth
links.reason: Gives wealth a gentle task, tending compassion as a foster-mother tends a child.

links.quote: Compassion, the child that loving-kindness bears
links.reason: Places compassion in a family, born of loving-kindness and brought up by wealth.

couplets.plain: Taking on a task with wealth in your hands is like watching elephants fight from the top of a hill.
couplets.pm: Taking up a task with wealth in hand is like climbing a hill to watch an elephant fight. The one on the hill, free of fear and trouble, sits at ease while elephants fight on the ground. So too the one with wealth, free of fear and trouble, sets skilled people to work and finishes the task at ease.

links.quote: Taking on a task with wealth in your hands
links.reason: Wealth lets you take up a task as calmly as a spectator on a height.

links.quote: from the top of a hill
links.reason: The hilltop is the safe place that wealth gives anyone who takes on a task.

links.quote: watching elephants fight
links.reason: The dangers of a task become a battle of elephants fought far below.

couplets.plain: Make wealth. There is no steel sharper for cutting your enemies’ pride.
couplets.pm: Those who want to get anything should make wealth. It is the weapon that cuts the pride of enemies, and no weapon is sharper. With wealth come a great army and allies, so enemies drop their pride and submit. Other steel can’t cut what has no form, so none is sharper.

links.quote: Make wealth
links.reason: Urges making wealth as the surest weapon against an enemy’s pride.

links.quote: no steel sharper

couplets.plain: For those who have made bright wealth in plenty, the other two come easily, and together.
couplets.pm: For those who have made wealth in great abundance by right means, the other two, righteousness and happiness, are easy to get, and come at the same time. Wealth is “bright” because it never goes without giving its fruit. The other two are its results, so they arise by themselves at once.

links.quote: made bright wealth in plenty
links.reason: With bright wealth made in plenty, the other aims of life stay within easy reach.

links.quote: the other two come easily, and together

ideaLinks.reason: Wealth gained without wrong gives birth to righteousness.

ideaLinks.quote: thrives with the rich foster-mother called wealth
ideaLinks.reason: Compassion needs wealth as a child needs a foster-mother to raise it.
